what: Pre-registration of the arms that serve Llama 3.1 Nemotron Safety Guard 8B v3 through its NIM; a supplement to the judge study's pre-registration
kept_from_the_study: the items and the subsets (results/p93_judges/items.jsonl, subsets.json), the labels, the two synthetic controls and the ten harmless prompts of the precheck, the answer parser, the definitions of every figure, greedy sampling, a new connection per direct call, the idle-card gate before every container start and every cell, and the scope rule: every figure is about one arm, and no per-item result of one arm is read together with a per-item result of another arm

why.what_the_study_did: arm J6 served this model with upstream vLLM 0.20.2 and called it 'not a NIM'. The NIM was not tried: the first sentence of its support matrix says the model requires 48 GB of GPU memory, and that sentence was taken as the answer.
why.what_was_not_read_then: the same support matrix lists a generic profile (vLLM, BF16, one GPU, 14.97 GB) that is not tied to a card model
why.question: does the model's NIM serve on this 32 GB card, and if it does, do the study's figures for this model change when only the serving package changes

documentation.release: NIM 1.14.0, built on NIM for LLMs 1.14.0
documentation.fp8_profiles: for RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition: FP8, TensorRT-LLM, 23.56 GB, one tuned for latency and one for throughput
documentation.known_issue: TensorRT-LLM profiles can have lower throughput under high load than the generic vLLM profile; for high concurrency and long sequences the release notes suggest the generic profile
documentation.official_parser: the example program reads the answer as JSON; an answer that does not parse is counted as unsafe

listing_on_this_card.what: `list-model-profiles` of the image on this RTX 5090, before any server was started
listing_on_this_card.reading: the image calls the generic profile compatible with this system and runnable, and both FP8 profiles incompatible with it; their names carry the device id 2bb5:10de, this card reports 2b85:10de
listing_on_this_card.also_printed: for every profile a warning that it does not support LoRA while LoRA is enabled; what that means for a start is not known before the run

prompt.reading: the study's prompt for this model (the model card's template) and the template of the NIM's documentation differ in one thing: each of the 23 category lines ends with a blank in the model card's and not in the documentation's. Nothing else differs on the conversations tested.

difference.checked_on: 4 conversations, with and without a response, one with line breaks, braces and trailing blanks, one in Chinese

guardrails.version: NeMo Guardrails 0.24.1 (the environment of the study)
guardrails.found_without_a_server: the configuration of the library's tutorial for a local NIM names the model twice (`model` and `parameters.model_name`); the library at the same tag refuses it: 'Model name must be specified in exactly one place'. With the name given once it is accepted, with engine `nim` as in the tutorial.

serving.start: docker run --gpus all --shm-size=64GB (the documentation's value), NIM_MODEL_PROFILE=<id>, NIM_MAX_MODEL_LEN=8192 (the context of the study's arm J6), port 8000 on 127.0.0.1, the NIM cache mounted
serving.not_set: the documentation's `-u $(id -u)` and `--runtime=nvidia` (the earlier NIM containers of this repository ran without them on this host)

download.how: `download-to-cache --profile <id>` in the image; not timed; what each call ended with is in the README of the results folder

nim_documentation.made_how: the model card's template with the blank removed from the end of each category line
nim_documentation.check: the runner refuses to start unless the template it derives renders the two test conversations to these values, which come from the documentation's own code

J6N.asked: as the study's arm J6: the model card's prompt in one user message, max_tokens 100, temperature 0.0, parsed by the study's parser
J6N.cells: per track: precheck, c=1 on the 200-item subset, c=16 on the whole track; in a new container the stability subset again (200 and 100 items)
J6N.one_variable_against: J6 of the study: the serving package (the NIM's vLLM instead of upstream vLLM 0.20.2). The program that asks and reads is the same file.

J6N-fp8.served_by: an FP8 TensorRT-LLM profile built for RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, pinned by id: the throughput profile first, the latency profile if that one does not report ready
J6N-fp8.against: J6N, and two things differ at once: the precision (FP8 for BF16) and the engine (TensorRT-LLM for vLLM). They are named as two and not told apart by this arm.

J6N-tpl.served_by: the generic profile, the same container as J6N
J6N-tpl.asked: as J6N with the documentation's template (23 blanks fewer)
J6N-tpl.cells: per track: precheck, c=1, c=16; no stability rerun
J6N-tpl.why_all_items: the work order asks for the 200-item subset; the whole track costs under a minute per track and lets the study's analysis program run unchanged

J6G.served_by: the generic profile, the same container as J6N
J6G.asked: through the NeMo Guardrails content-safety rail, one call at a time, on the study's subset for the Guardrails path (100 items per track)
J6G.configuration: the library's tutorial for this model at tag v0.24.1 (engine nim, model type content_safety, the two content-safety flows) with its prompts file byte for byte: max_tokens 50, parsers nemoguard_parse_*
changes_from_the_tutorial: the base URL is the local server's
the model name is given once
the main model points at the same server and is never called (no answer is generated in this study)
J6G.recorded: per item the rail's decision and, apart from it, the verdict the study's parser reads from the same completion; each item is classed by its own two readings (no other arm is read)

guardrails.source: examples/configs/content_safety_multilingual/prompts.yml of NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails at tag v0.24.1; equal to the prompts block of the tutorial docs/getting-started/tutorials/nemotron-safety-guard-deployment.mdx at the same tag

reference_figures_of_the_study_arm_J6.served_by: upstream vLLM 0.20.2, BF16; 30.3 GiB of the card in use once ready

from_the_work_order.J6N: starts; detection and false alarm inside the Wilson intervals of J6; verdicts per second at c=16 within 15% of J6
from_the_work_order.J6N-fp8: an even chance that it does not start; if it starts, detection within 2 points of J6N

added_here.J6N: c=1 p50 within 15% of J6's (204.1 ms input, 295.4 ms output); stability at least 98%
added_here.J6N-fp8: does not report ready (about 70%): the image itself lists both FP8 profiles as incompatible with this system, by device id
added_here.J6N-tpl: detection and false alarm within 1 point of J6N on every data set: the prompts differ by 23 blanks
added_here.J6G: the rail blocks both violating controls and allows both harmless ones. Among the 100 items of a track a few (0 to 10) are blocked although the study's parser reads their completion as safe: the prompts file sets max_tokens 50, J6's answers reach more than that on some items (p99 of its output tokens is in the reference figures), a cut JSON object does not parse, and the library's parser counts that as unsafe
added_here.confidence: moderate for J6N; low for the others

branches_decided_in_advance.J6N reports ready: its figures stand beside J6's; whether it replaces J6 in the main table and the figures is decided by the people who write the article
branches_decided_in_advance.J6N does not report ready: the reason, the first error line and the profile listing are the result; J6 stays as it is
branches_decided_in_advance.J6N-fp8 reports ready: one more line, labelled 'FP8 TensorRT-LLM profile built for RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, pinned on an RTX 5090', with both differences named
branches_decided_in_advance.J6N-fp8 does not report ready: one sentence and the error text
branches_decided_in_advance.J6G's rail decision differs from the ver: each such item is listed by id and class (answer cut, answer unreadable, library raised); the configuration is not changed to make them agree
branches_decided_in_advance.a precheck fails: that arm and track is null, as in the study

not_in_this_file: any change to the study's figures or files
the documentation example's request parameters (max_tokens 2048, top_p 1) as an arm of their own
programs_written_after_the_freeze: none planned; if one is needed, its SHA-256 is written to the events file before its first use
